Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with real simple roots (so $a_{ii}=2$ for
every color $i$), a field $k$ placed in degree zero, and weighted-homogeneous
KLR polynomials $Q_{jk}$ satisfying (Q1)-(Q4) as in
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]; write
$b_{jk}=d_j a_{jk}=b_{kj}$. Fix a color $i$. The **minimal-parabolic KLR
diagram proof category** $\mathcal P_i$ is the additive graded $k$-linear
2-category of weighted oriented diagrams described by the generators, objects
and equations below.

**Generators and composition.** The objects are the weights
$\mu\in P$. The generating $1$-morphisms are the downward generators
$G_j:\mu\to\mu-\alpha_j$, one for every color $j$, and the single upward
generator $H_i:\mu\to\mu+\alpha_i$. Horizontal composition reads chronological
negative words from the vacuum outward. Take additive sums of objects and
grading shifts, and use idempotent completion when speaking of word
projectives. The generator $H_i$ denotes **normalized projective
restriction**: in the polynomial flag realization at input weight $h=\langle
h_i,\mu\rangle$ it is basic reversed flag restriction shifted by
$-d_i(1+h)$; it is distinct from unshifted basic restriction.

**The graded 2-morphism spaces.** The weights are 0-objects. A 1-morphism
is a finite composable word in the $G_j,H_i$, with its specified source and
target weights; identities are empty words. For parallel words $u,v$, define
$\operatorname{Hom}^n(u,v)$ as the degree-$n$ part of the $k$-span of formal
oriented string diagrams generated by the dots, downward crossings and four
units/counits below, modulo the displayed local relations. Every strand is
labeled by its color, and its direction is downward for $G_j$ and upward for
$H_i$. The top boundary is the source word and the bottom boundary the target
word. Regions carry the unique weights obtained from the outside source
weight by the indicated simple-root changes. Diagrams are generic: transverse
double crossings, isolated dots and nondegenerate cups/caps, with no triple
crossing or dot at a crossing/extremum. Oppositely oriented crossings denote
the specified adjunction mates of a downward crossing, not new generators.
Use planar isotopies preserving the ordered oriented local events; moving
a crossing past an extremum uses the mate relations below. Vertical
composition is stacking and horizontal composition is juxtaposition at a
common weight; degrees add under either operation. The interchange relation
and bilinearity are imposed. A degree-$n$ map from $u$ to $v$ is a degree-zero
map $u\{n\}\to v$ with the internal-shift convention of the grading supplier.
Additive sums, shifts and idempotent completion have their usual graded
2-category meanings applied to these Hom spaces.

**Degrees and the native crossing.** Dots have degree $2d_j$ and downward
crossings have degree $-b_{jk}$, matching the grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]. The native crossing is
$\tau$, with native equal-color divided difference
$(f-sf)/(x_1-x_2)$; for expressing the source diagram equations put
$\kappa=-\tau$ for **every** color pair, retaining dots, idempotents and $Q$.
Thus the native cubic braid numerator is globally opposite to the source
numerator, while the quadratic $Q$ is unchanged. Impose the full downward KLR
relations of the cited Definition.

**Adjunctions and the rank-one matrix.** At input $i$-weight $h$, the first
unit $1\to H_iG_i$ and the second counit $H_iG_i\to1$ have degree
$d_i(1-h)$; the first counit $G_iH_i\to1$ and the second unit
$1\to G_iH_i$ have degree $d_i(1+h)$. Impose both adjunction triangles with
their adjacent input-weight shifts and cyclicity of the dot. For $h\ge0$
prescribe the degree-zero rank-one matrix
$$H_iG_i\cong G_iH_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{h-1}1\{d_i(1-h+2r)\};$$
for $h<0$ prescribe
$$G_iH_i\cong H_iG_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{-h-1}1\{d_i(1+h+2r)\}.$$
The off-diagonal crossing component is the cup--source-crossing--cap
transfer, and the identity columns and rows are the indicated dotted
units/counits. Adjoin its actual inverse blocks, requiring both matrix inverse
equations; the dotted dual rows and columns are the finite triangular
coefficient convolution determined by bubble inversion, and the crossing
block satisfies the local cross-and-cap equations. In particular, at $h<0$,
if $r_h:G_iH_i\to H_iG_i\oplus D_{-h}$ is this matrix, then $r_h^{-1}j_H$ and
$p_Hr_h$ are the specified natural inclusion and projection with product
$1_{H_iG_i}$.

**Explicit rank-one inverse blocks.** Put $P=G_iH_i$, $V=H_iG_i$
at the common outside weight $\mu$, and write
$\eta_\mu:1_\mu\to H_iG_i$, $\varepsilon_\mu:G_iH_i\to1_\mu$
for the first adjunction and
$\eta'_\mu:1_\mu\to G_iH_i$, $\varepsilon'_\mu:H_iG_i\to1_\mu$
for the second. Let $\tau^{GG}$ be the native equal-color downward crossing
and $\tau^{HH}$ its twofold adjunction mate. Fix the native sideways mates by
$$T=(H_iG_i\varepsilon_\mu)(H_i\tau^{GG}H_i)(\eta_\mu G_iH_i),\qquad S=(G_iH_i\varepsilon'_\mu)(G_i\tau^{HH}G_i)(\eta'_\mu H_iG_i).$$
Their middle words are respectively $H_iG_iG_iH_i$ and
$G_iH_iH_iG_i$; the displayed final counits consume their rightmost
$G_iH_i$ and $H_iG_i$. Thus $T:P\to V$ and $S:V\to P$ are typed,
with degree $d_i(1-h)-2d_i+d_i(1+h)=0$. The source-crossing
component in the preceding rank-one matrix is $-T$. For $h\ge0$, its
identity columns are $C_k=x^k\eta_\mu$, and its identity rows are
$$R_k=\sum_{a+j=h-1-k}A_{\mu,j}\,\varepsilon'_\mu x^a,\qquad 0\le k<h,$$
where $a,j\ge0$. The matrix is $\rho=(-T,(C_k)_k):P\oplus D_h\to V$
and its specified inverse is $\sigma=(S,(R_k)_k):V\to P\oplus D_h$.
Impose both equations $\sigma\rho=1$ and $\rho\sigma=1$; in components
these say $-ST=1_P$, $R_kT=0$, $SC_k=0$, $R_kC_\ell=\delta_{k\ell}$
and $-TS+\sum_kC_kR_k=1_V$. For $h<0$, take
$C^-_k=x^k\eta'_\mu$ and
$$R^-_k=\sum_{a+j=-h-1-k}\mathsf H_{\mu,j}\,\varepsilon_\mu x^a,\qquad 0\le k<-h,$$
again with $a,j\ge0$. Now
$\rho=(-T,(R^-_k)_k):P\to V\oplus D_{-h}$ and
$\sigma=(S,(C^-_k)_k):V\oplus D_{-h}\to P$; impose
$\rho\sigma=1$, $\sigma\rho=1$. Equivalently $-TS=1_V$,
$TC^-_k=0$, $R^-_kS=0$, $R^-_kC^-_\ell=\delta_{k\ell}$ and
$-ST+\sum_kC^-_kR^-_k=1_P$. The shift summands $D_h,D_{-h}$ are
exactly those displayed above. The row degrees are respectively
$d_i(h-1-2k)$ and $-d_i(1+h+2k)$, opposite the column degrees, so every
matrix component is degree zero after the indicated shifts. Empty identity
sums at $h=0$ give the same inverse equations. These are imposed relations
in the presentation; a claim that the concrete flag bimodules satisfy them
still requires their local realization proof.

**Bubble series and slides.** The normalized far-left bubble series
$A_\mu(t),\mathsf H_\mu(t)$ have constant coefficient $1$ and satisfy
$A_\mu(t)\mathsf H_\mu(t)=1$. Genuine negative-degree bubbles vanish. The $A$
coefficient with index $m$ is the clockwise bubble with $-h-1+m$ dots when
this count is nonnegative, extended by formal inverse coefficients otherwise;
its degree is $2d_im$. The other family has dot count $h-1+\ell$ and degree
$2d_i\ell$. Impose the finite-coefficient slides verified on the monic flag
model: adjoining an $i$ root $z$ divides $A$ by $(1-zt)^2$ and multiplies
$\mathsf H$ by that factor; adjoining a spectator root $y$ of color $j\ne i$
multiplies $A$ by
$q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}(y,t)=t^{-a_{ij}}Q_{ij}(t^{-1},y)/t_{ij}$, where $t_{ij}$
is the nonzero extremal coefficient, and divides $\mathsf H$ by it. Every
reciprocal coefficient is defined by the finite recursion with constant
coefficient $1$.

**Four oriented same-color equations.** The following notation specifies
actual local diagrams, all with color $i$. The two-crossing equations have
common outside weight $\mu$; the single curls have the adjacent region
weights specified individually below.
Read tangent directions in the page. Let $C_L,C_R$ be the cap arch
(two bottom endpoints and no top endpoints), whose tangent at its peak
points left or right, respectively. Their bottom arrows, from left to
right, are $(\downarrow,\uparrow)$ and
$(\uparrow,\downarrow)$. Let $U_L,U_R$ be the cup valley
(two top endpoints and no bottom endpoints), whose tangent at its trough
points left or right; their top arrows are
$(\uparrow,\downarrow)$ and $(\downarrow,\uparrow)$.
An exponent on $C$ or $U$ counts dots on its open arc. Let $B_{\mathrm{ccw}}^b$
and $B_{\mathrm{cw}}^b$ be the counterclockwise and clockwise bubbles
with literal dot count $b$, located to the right of the cap/cup in the outside
region of weight $\mu$. Their negative dot counts are exactly the fake
bubbles defined by the coefficient conventions above, not zero by convention.
Write $\eta_\mu:1_\mu\to H_iG_i$ and
$\varepsilon'_\mu:H_iG_i\to1_\mu$ for the first unit and second counit,
and $\eta'_\mu:1_\mu\to G_iH_i$, $\varepsilon_\mu:G_iH_i\to1_\mu$
for the second unit and first counit. Let $\tau^{HH}$ be the twofold
adjunction mate of the native equal-color downward crossing. Define
$$L_\mu=(H_i\varepsilon'_\mu)(\tau^{HH}G_i)(H_i\eta_\mu),\qquad R_\mu=(\varepsilon_\mu H_i)(G_i\tau^{HH})(\eta'_\mu H_i).$$
The first formula starts and ends at $H_i$ with input $\mu$; the second
starts and ends at $H_i$ with input $\mu-\alpha_i$. Thus both units and
counits in $L_\mu$ have degree $d_i(1-h)$, while those in $R_\mu$ have
degree $d_i(1+h)$. The crossing degree $-2d_i$ makes their degrees
$-2d_ih$ and $2d_ih$ respectively. Products in these formulas apply the
rightmost map first, with adjacent weights determined by composition.
Geometrically $L_\mu$ is an upward-strand curl with its loop bulging LEFT and
its left-adjacent region of weight $\mu$. This is an endomorphism of
$H_i$ at input $\mu$, and its bubble on the right-hand side is in the
left region $\mu$. Let $R_\mu$ be the upward-strand curl with its loop
bulging RIGHT and its right-adjacent region of weight $\mu$. Its left
region is $\mu-\alpha_i$, so it is an endomorphism of $H_i$ at input
$\mu-\alpha_i$, and its bubble is in the right region $\mu$.
Both have one native crossing and the two extremal turns of the loop.
Let $D_{\downarrow\uparrow}$ and $D_{\uparrow\downarrow}$ be the two
opposite crossing mates composed in the two orders on their indicated
straight boundaries, with common outside region $\mu$. Impose
$$L_\mu=\sum_{a+b=-1}x^aB_{\mathrm{ccw},\mu}^b,\qquad R_\mu=-\sum_{a+b=-1}x^aB_{\mathrm{cw},\mu}^b,$$
$$D_{\downarrow\uparrow}=-1_{\downarrow\uparrow}+\sum_{a+b+c=-2}C_L^aB_{\mathrm{cw},\mu}^bU_R^c,$$
$$D_{\uparrow\downarrow}=-1_{\uparrow\downarrow}+\sum_{a+b+c=-2}C_R^aB_{\mathrm{ccw},\mu}^bU_L^c.$$
Composition in the last two displays is top-to-bottom: $U$ first, then
the outside bubble, then $C$. The single-curl equations are upward-strand
endomorphism equations; their cup/cap forms are their specified adjunction
mates, not cap drawings with unspecified endpoint arrows. In every sum,
$a,c$ on open strands are nonnegative. The clockwise bubble with literal
$b$ dots is the $A_\mu$ coefficient of index $b+h+1$, and the
counterclockwise bubble is the $\mathsf H_\mu$ coefficient of index
$b-h+1$, where $h=\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$. Coefficients of negative index
are zero and the index-zero coefficient is one. The nonnegative coefficient
and open-dot indices make each sum finite. The opposite-crossing equations
have degree zero: their correction degrees are
$2d_i(1-h)+2d_i(a+b+c+h+1)=0$ and
$2d_i(1+h)+2d_i(a+b+c-h+1)=0$. The two curls have degrees
$-2d_ih$ and $2d_ih$ at their respective, different input weights.

The native single-crossing signs follow from $\kappa=-\tau$; two-crossing
signs are unchanged. The literal triple-dot sum is $-2$, not the compact
$-1$ printed in Webster's Figure 2: in the full positive-weight equation,
coefficient indices satisfy $f_1+f_2+f_3=h-1$ and the bubble has literal
count $b=-h-1+f_2$, giving $a+b+c=-2$; the negative-weight equation uses
$g_1+g_2+g_3=-h-1$ and $b=h-1+g_2$, giving the same value. Reflection
exchanges the two bubble orientations and preserves region weights. The
single-curl coefficient sums instead have total $h$ or $-h$, yielding
literal $a+b=-1$. At $h=0$ the triple sums are empty and the single
curls are respectively $+1$ and $-1$ on their specified shifted input
weights. At the $h=1$, $p(u)=u$ vacuum, $H_iG_i=k$, $G_iH_i=0$,
$A_\mu=1$ and the only surviving clockwise bubble has $b=-2$; thus the
first cancellation is $0=-1_k+1_k$, with no degree or vacuum contradiction.

**Distinct-color crossing mates.** For $j\ne i$, at input weight $\mu$
put $\xi=\mu+\alpha_i-\alpha_j$, so $X=G_jH_i$ and $Y=H_iG_j$
both go from $\mu$ to $\xi$. Let $\tau^{G_iG_j}:G_iG_j\to G_jG_i$
and $\tau^{G_jG_i}:G_jG_i\to G_iG_j$ denote the two native downward
crossings. Specify the handed pair by the actual typed mate composites
$$a=(H_iG_j\varepsilon_\mu)(H_i\tau^{G_iG_j}H_i)(\eta_\xi G_jH_i):X\to Y,$$
$$b=(\varepsilon'_\xi G_jH_i)(H_i\tau^{G_jG_i}H_i)(H_iG_j\eta'_\mu):Y\to X.$$
The intermediate words are respectively $H_iG_iG_jH_i$ and
$H_iG_jG_iH_i$; in $a$ the final first counit consumes the rightmost
$G_iH_i$, while in $b$ the final second counit consumes the leftmost
$H_iG_i$. Impose $ba=t_{ij}1_X$ and $ab=t_{ij}1_Y$ for this same handed
pair. Thus $a$ and $t_{ij}^{-1}b$ are mutually inverse and give
$H_iG_j\cong G_jH_i$, commuting with the $j$ dot. If
$h=\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$, both composites have degree
$d_i(1+h)+d_i(-1-h+a_{ij})-b_{ij}=0$. Replacing both native crossings by
the source crossings $\kappa=-\tau$ negates $a$ and $b$ separately and
leaves both cancellation scalars unchanged.

There is no $H_j$ in this minimal category. The analogous calculation in
the separately distinguished category $\mathcal P_j$ has scalar $t_{ji}$
in both orders for its own handed pair. That does not assign $t_{ji}$ to
the other composition of the fixed pair $a,b$ above. Comparing the two
partial actions, or asserting a full double-right-mate ratio, requires the
separate coherent assembly proof; it is not an additional relation imposed
here.

**Status of the relations.** These equations are relations of this proof-tool
category. Their consistency and homogeneous realization are established by
the polynomial flag model
([[lem-minimal-parabolic-polynomial-flag-model-realizes-the-graded-diagram-relations]]),
rather than assumed for the actual cyclotomic induction/restriction action; no
claim about the latter is made here. This definition uses no choice: it is a
presentation by generators and homogeneous equations, and every sl(2) infinite
family appearing in the matrix and bubble clauses is a finite coefficient
recursion from a constant coefficient $1$.

Let $p(u)$ be monic of degree $N\geq0$ over a commutative ring $D$. Let $L_r$ be the monic factor ring $p=c_rb_{N-r}$, where $c_r$ is monic of degree $r$, and put $L_r=0$ for $r<0$ or $r>N$. Put
$$B_r=L_r[z]/b_{N-r}(z)=L_{r+1}[z]/c_{r+1}(z),\qquad h=N-2r.$$
Use the native nil-Hecke crossing $\tau=(1-s)/(X-Y)$ of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], dots of degree $2d$, and the matrix idempotent convention of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. Induction is $G(r)=B_r\{-2dr\}\otimes_{L_r}-$, basic restriction is the reversed $B_{r-1}$ tensor functor, and normalized restriction at input $r$ is $H(r)=B_{r-1}\{-d(1+h)\}\otimes_{L_r}-$. The first adjunction uses the coefficient form $\tau_{\rm new}:B_r\to L_{r+1}$ extracting $z^r$; the second uses $\tau_{\rm old}:B_r\to L_r$ extracting $z^{N-r-1}$. Units are the trace-dual power-basis Casimirs. Write $\eta:1\to HG$, $\varepsilon:GH\to1$, $\eta':1\to GH$, $\varepsilon':HG\to1$ for these maps, at their indicated input weights.

Set $P=GH$, $V=HG$ at input $r$. Define the actual native mates, rather than freely adjoined inverses, by
$$T=(HG\varepsilon)(H\tau^{GG}H)(\eta GH):P\to V,\qquad S=(GH\varepsilon')(G\tau^{HH}G)(\eta'HG):V\to P,$$
where $\tau^{HH}$ is the twofold first-adjunction mate of $\tau^{GG}$. Put
$$A(t)=t^h\frac{b(t^{-1})}{c(t^{-1})},\qquad \mathsf H(t)=A(t)^{-1},\qquad A_0=\mathsf H_0=1.$$
Coefficients with negative index are zero. For $h\geq0$, let $C_k=x^k\eta$ and
$$R_k=\sum_{a+j=h-1-k}A_j\varepsilon'x^a\quad(0\leq k<h).$$
Then the actual flag bimodule maps $\rho=(-T,C):P\oplus D_h\to V$ and $\sigma=(S,R):V\to P\oplus D_h$ satisfy
$$-ST=1_P,\quad R_kT=0,\quad SC_k=0,\quad R_kC_\ell=\delta_{k\ell},\quad -TS+\sum_kC_kR_k=1_V.$$
For $h<0$, set $C^-_k=x^k\eta'$ and
$$R^-_k=\sum_{a+j=-h-1-k}\mathsf H_j\varepsilon x^a\quad(0\leq k<-h).$$
The maps $\rho=(-T,R^-):P\to V\oplus D_{-h}$ and $\sigma=(S,C^-):V\oplus D_{-h}\to P$ satisfy
$$-TS=1_V,\quad TC^-_k=0,\quad R^-_kS=0,\quad R^-_kC^-_\ell=\delta_{k\ell},\quad -ST+\sum_kC^-_kR^-_k=1_P.$$
Here $D_h=\bigoplus_{k<h}1\{d(1-h+2k)\}$ and $D_{-h}=\bigoplus_{k<-h}1\{d(1+h+2k)\}$. At $h=0$ both sums are empty.

These maps also give the two typed upward curls
$$L_\mu=(H\varepsilon'_\mu)(\tau^{HH}G)(H\eta_\mu),\qquad R_\mu=(\varepsilon_\mu H)(G\tau^{HH})(\eta'_\mu H),$$
where $L_\mu$ has input $\mu$ and $R_\mu$ input $\mu-\alpha_i$, with $\langle h_i,\mu\rangle=h$. Their formulas are
$$L_\mu=\sum_{a+j=-h}x^a\mathsf H_j,\qquad R_\mu=-\sum_{a+j=h}x^aA_j.$$
All indices in these sums are nonnegative. Mating the two matrix-completeness equations gives the two opposite-crossing cancellation equations with literal-dot sum $a+b+c=-2$: the $HG$ boundary uses $A_{b+h+1}$, and the $GH$ boundary uses $\mathsf H_{b-h+1}$. Single curls instead have literal-dot sum $a+b=-1$.

For a symmetrizable datum and distinguished color $i$, take a dominant integral framing $\lambda_i\geq0$ and
$$p(u)=a_i(u)\prod_{j\ne i}\prod_{y\in Y_j}Q_{ij}(u,y)/t_{ij},\qquad t_{ij}=[u^{-a_{ij}}]Q_{ij}(u,y)\in D^\times.$$
This realizes every $r\geq0$, including both signs of $h$, with zero modules past $N$. Appending a color $j$ root uses the quotient and multiplication by $Q_{ij}$, and the mixed mate pair constructed with the first unit/first cap and second unit/second cap has composites $t_{ij}$ in **both** orders. This identifies the actual mixed mates in the distinguished-$i$ flag model. Compatibility with adjunctions for a second distinguished color is a separate assembly question.

Under the nil-Hecke matrix equivalence the first cap is exactly $\tau_{\rm new}$ and the normalized relative second cap is exactly $\tau_{\rm old}$: the normalization is $\widehat\varepsilon_r=(-1)^{N+1}\varepsilon_r$ for the ordered-residue relative form defined in the proof. No formal diagram-model realization, categorical commutator, cyclotomic Frobenius theorem, or one-dimensional Hom hypothesis is a premise. Every assertion is an integral polynomial identity, hence survives arbitrary monic specialization. Grading is asserted only when the coefficients are homogeneous in their natural degrees.

For the formal category $\mathcal P_i$ of
[[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], fix one reduced
perfect-matching diagram for each compatible boundary matching, one dot
position on each component, and the positive normalized far-left bubble family
$A_\mu(t)=1+\sum_{m>0}A_{\mu,m}t^m$. These matching diagrams multiplied by
open-component dot monomials and monomials in the $A_{\mu,m}$ form a basis.
There is a finite straightening procedure with this output; its coefficients
are independent of all choices of permissible straightening moves. At
all-downward boundaries its basis is the ordinary KLR PBW basis tensored with
$k[A_{\mu,1},A_{\mu,2},\ldots]$. The universal graded polynomial flag models
are jointly faithful at every fixed physical source weight.

Let $\Lambda$ be dominant, let $a_j(u)$ be monic of degree
$\lambda_j=\langle h_j,\Lambda\rangle$, and let $J$ be the representable
ideal generated by $1_{H_iv_\Lambda}$ and
$a_j(x)1_{G_jv_\Lambda}$, closed under vertical compositions and all allowed
horizontal whiskers. For downward words $u,v$ of weight difference $\beta$,
$$J\cap e(v)R(\beta)e(u)=e(v)I_a(\beta)e(u),\qquad I_a(\beta)=\sum_jR(\beta)a_j(x_1)e(j,\beta-\alpha_j)R(\beta).$$
The vacuum specialization is $A_\Lambda=a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}$ and
$\mathsf H_\Lambda=A_\Lambda^{-1}$. The downward Hom corners of
$\mathcal P_i(\Lambda)/J$ are therefore exactly the ordinary monic
cyclotomic corners. Here the corner $e(v)R e(u)$ acts as a map $e(u)R	o e(v)R$ between right projectives. Every word in this quotient is a retract of a finite
sum of downward words. Consequently its additive idempotent completion is
equivalent to the category of finite right cyclotomic word projectives, with $G_j$
acting by actual word induction. The first adjunction identifies $H_i$ with
the corresponding normalized projective restriction; the second adjunction
maps transport through this equivalence as actual natural transformations.

These assertions hold for every degree-zero field and every admissible
homogeneous $Q$. The monic deformation is first taken over the universal
graded coefficient ring; arbitrary monic field specializations assert the
ungraded conclusions. No cyclotomic Frobenius theorem is assumed.

Use the standard graded cyclotomic quotient of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], and keep the conventions
fixed there: the cyclotomic relation is imposed on the FIRST strand and
cyclotomic induction appends strands on the RIGHT. Fix $\beta\in Q_+$ and a
color $i$; put
$$A:=R^\Lambda(\beta),\qquad B:=R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i),\qquad e:=e(\beta,i),$$
where $e(\beta,i)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(\nu i)\in R(\beta+\alpha_i)$ is the
idempotent of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]
supported on the sequences ending in $i$.

**The right-append corner homomorphism.** Right append defines a
$k$-algebra homomorphism
$$\iota_i:A\longrightarrow eBe,\qquad 1_A\longmapsto e,\quad e(\nu)\longmapsto e(\nu i),\quad x_a\longmapsto x_a,\quad \tau_a\longmapsto\tau_a ,$$
sending each old dot or crossing to the same-named generator at the same
position in the first $|\beta|$ strands of $R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$ and
each old idempotent to the longer idempotent obtained by appending $i$. It is
a graded homomorphism of degree zero: each generic relation (1)-(7) of
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] is preserved
under right append, and the first-strand cyclotomic generator of $A$ maps to
the first-strand cyclotomic generator of $B$, so the cyclotomic relation is
preserved and $\iota_i$ is well defined on the quotient. The unit is sent to
the corner unit $e$, not to a global unit of $B$; it is **not** asserted that
$\iota_i$ is injective, and $e$ is allowed to be zero.

**The functors.** On graded left modules define
$$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(M):=Be\otimes_A M,\qquad E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(N):=eN,$$
the tensor over the graded balanced tensor product of
[[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]] and the idempotent
restriction of the graded $B$-module $N$
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]). Both are additive
$k$-linear functors between the graded module categories, they preserve
degree-zero maps, and they extend to direct sums over the root degrees
$\beta\in Q_+$.

**Adjunction, weights and shifts.** Evaluation at $e$ identifies
$\operatorname{HOM}_B(Be,N)$ with $eN$ by the degree-zero tensor--Hom
adjunction, giving $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ with its
actual grading. The functor $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ increases ROOT degree by
$\alpha_i$, taking modules at root $\beta$ to modules at root
$\beta+\alpha_i$, and decreases the module weight $\Lambda-\beta$ by
$\alpha_i$; restriction does the reverse. Both composites are endofunctors at
a fixed root degree. Grading shifts satisfy
$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(M\{r\})\cong F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(M)\{r\}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(N\{r\})\cong E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(N)\{r\}$, using the
internal shifts of [[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]].

**Ungraded monic deformations.** For a general monic
specialization $a_j(u)$ the quotient $R^\Lambda_a(\beta)$ of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]] carries no grading, and
the same formulas define the ungraded functors $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$; no graded statement is asserted on that branch.

**Status of further structure.** Exactness, preservation of projectives and a
shifted second adjunction are theorems below, not part of this definition; in
particular no unshifted right adjunction $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv
F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ is asserted here, and the explicit shift of the second
adjunction is supplied by the coherent-biadjunction lemma of this page. This
definition uses no choice.

Let $R^\Lambda$ be the cyclotomic KLR algebra of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], and let
$E^\Lambda_i,F^\Lambda_i$ be the functors of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]]. For every $i\in I$
and $\beta\in Q_+$:

(a) the bimodule $R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,i)$ is a projective right
$R^\Lambda(\beta)$-module, and $e(\beta,i)R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$ is a
projective left $R^\Lambda(\beta)$-module;

(b) consequently $E^\Lambda_i$ and $F^\Lambda_i$ are exact and send finitely
generated graded projectives to finitely generated graded projectives;
moreover $F^\Lambda_i$ preserves all projectives and $E^\Lambda_i$ preserves
finitely generated ones;

(c) there is a functorial exact sequence in
$\mathrm{Mod}(R(\beta+\alpha_i))$
$$0\longrightarrow q^{(\alpha_i\mid 2\Lambda-\beta)}\bar F_iM\longrightarrow F_iM\longrightarrow F^\Lambda_iM\longrightarrow 0,\qquad M\in\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta)),$$
where $F_i$ is the right-append and $\bar F_i$ the left-append generic
induction of
[[lem-generic-klr-induction-and-restriction-mixed-relations]], regarded on
$R^\Lambda$-modules through the quotient, and the exponent is the Cartan
pairing $(\alpha_i\mid 2\Lambda-\beta)=2(\alpha_i\mid\Lambda)
-(\alpha_i\mid\beta)$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] records the
normalization of the powers of $q$).

**Total internal degree on the balanced tensor product.** Let $A$ be a graded
$k$-algebra, $M$ a graded right $A$-module and $N$ a graded left $A$-module
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]). First use the canonical
decomposition of the ordinary tensor product of the underlying abelian groups
$$M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N\cong\bigoplus_{i,j\in\mathbb Z}M_i\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N_j.$$
Its inverse sends $m\otimes n$ to the finite sum
$\sum_{i,j}m_i\otimes n_j$, where $m=\sum_i m_i$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are their
homogeneous decompositions; the two maps are inverse because they agree with
the identity on homogeneous elementary tensors. Give the summand
$M_i\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N_j$ total degree $i+j$, and write
$G_d:=\bigoplus_{i+j=d}M_i\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N_j$.

The balanced tensor product
$M\otimes_AN=(M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N)/\mathcal R_A$
([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]), where
$\mathcal R_A$ is generated by the balance relations
$(ma)\otimes n-m\otimes(an)$. These relations are generated by the homogeneous
ones: for $m=\sum_i m_i$, $a=\sum_\ell a_\ell$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$, the relation
is the finite sum of
$(m_i a_\ell)\otimes n_j-m_i\otimes(a_\ell n_j)$ over $i,\ell,j$. Each such
homogeneous relation belongs to $G_{i+\ell+j}$, since the two module actions
preserve total degree. Thus $\mathcal R_A=\bigoplus_d(\mathcal R_A\cap G_d)$,
and

$$M\otimes_AN=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}(M\otimes_AN)_d,\qquad (M\otimes_AN)_d:=(G_d+\mathcal R_A)/\mathcal R_A,$$

is a graded abelian group. For homogeneous $m\in M_i$ and $n\in N_j$ the
elementary tensor $m\otimes n$ has **total internal degree** $i+j$; every tensor
is a finite sum of homogeneous elementary tensors, and the balancing relations
used in the quotient are homogeneous. This grading is the only grading used
below, and it introduces no sign.

**Outer actions.** If $M$ is a graded $(B,A)$-bimodule and $N$ a graded left
$A$-module, then the action $b(m\otimes n):=(bm)\otimes n$ of
[[thm-bimodule-actions-induced-on-tensor-products]] makes $M\otimes_AN$ a graded
left $B$-module: the action is homogeneous because homogeneous $b\in B_l$ sends
$m\otimes n$ of degree $i+j$ to an element of degree $l+i+j$. Symmetrically, if
$N$ is a graded $(A,C)$-bimodule, the action
$(m\otimes n)c:=m\otimes(nc)$ makes $M\otimes_AN$ a graded right $C$-module, and
the two outer actions commute when both are present.

**Homogeneous Hom.** For graded left $A$-modules $P,Q$, with
$\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(P,Q)$ the abelian group of all $A$-linear
maps $P\to Q$, put

$$\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,Q):=\bigl\{f\in\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(P,Q)\mid f(P_i)\subseteq Q_{i+d}\ \text{for all }i\in\mathbb Z\bigr\},\qquad \operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q):=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,Q).$$

Each $\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,Q)$ is a subgroup of
$\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(P,Q)$, and the sum is direct: if
$f=\sum_df_d=\sum_df'_d$ with $f_d,f'_d\in\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}$, then for
$p\in P_i$ the element $f(p)$ has homogeneous components
$f_d(p)\in Q_{i+d}$, and comparison of the graded components in $Q$ gives
$f_d(p)=f'_d(p)$ for every $d$ and $p$, so $f_d=f'_d$. Thus
$\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q)$ is a graded abelian group whose degree-$d$ part is
$\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,Q)$, and the degree-zero morphisms are
$\operatorname{Hom}_{A,0}(P,Q)$. By definition $\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q)$
consists of the finite sums of homogeneous $A$-linear maps, so
$\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q)\subseteq\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(P,Q)$
with equality only when every $A$-linear map has bounded spread in degree.

**The associative left action.** If $M$ is a graded $(B,A)$-bimodule and $Y$ a
graded left $B$-module, then $\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,Y)$ carries a left
$A$-module structure

$$(a\cdot f)(m):=f(ma)\qquad(a\in A,\ m\in M),$$

which is homogeneous: for $a\in A_i$ and $f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{B,d}(M,Y)$ one
has $ma\in M_{l+i}$ for $m\in M_l$, hence $(a\cdot f)(m)\in Y_{l+i+d}$ and
$a\cdot f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{B,d+i}(M,Y)$. The action is associative and
unital by the module axioms of $M$, so $\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,Y)$ is a graded
left $A$-module and an object of $\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$. The same formula
defines an action on the full ungraded $\operatorname{Hom}$ group, where it is
denoted by the same symbol.

**Ground ring and graded algebras.** Fix a commutative ring $k$. A **graded
$k$-algebra** is a $k$-algebra $A$ in the sense of
[[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]], together with a direct sum
decomposition of $k$-modules

$$A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb Z}A_i$$

such that $A_iA_j\subseteq A_{i+j}$ for all $i,j\in\mathbb Z$ and
$1_A\in A_0$. It is **unital and associative** when its underlying ring is;
every graded algebra on this page is unital and associative. Since
$\eta_A(r)=r\,1_A$ and $A_0$ is a $k$-submodule containing $1_A$, the structure
map has image in $A_0$, so each $A_i$ is a $k$-submodule and the scalars act
centrally on $A$.

**Graded modules and bimodules.** A **graded left $A$-module** is a left
$A$-module $M$ with a decomposition $M=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}M_d$ of
$k$-modules such that

$$A_iM_d\subseteq M_{i+d}\qquad\text{for all }i,d\in\mathbb Z .$$

A **graded right $A$-module** is a right $A$-module with a decomposition
$M=\bigoplus_dM_d$ such that $M_dA_i\subseteq M_{d+i}$ for all $i,d$. A
**graded $(B,A)$-bimodule** is a $(B,A)$-bimodule ([[def-bimodule]]) that is
graded as a $k$-module and homogeneous under both actions, the two actions
continuing to commute. Both induced $k$-actions must agree with the given
$k$-module structure: $\eta_B(t)m=tm=m\eta_A(t)$ for $t\in k$ and $m\in M$. Elements of $M_d$ are **homogeneous of degree $d$**, and
the decomposition expresses every $m\in M$ uniquely as a finite sum of nonzero
homogeneous components.

**Degree-zero maps.** A map $f:M\to N$ of graded left $A$-modules is
**degree-zero**, or a **graded map**, when it is $A$-linear and
$f(M_d)\subseteq N_d$ for every $d$. The category $\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$
has the graded left $A$-modules as objects and the degree-zero maps as
morphisms, with composition of maps. Every $M$ is an object of
$\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$ by its own grading, and $A$ is a graded
$(A,A)$-bimodule under left and right multiplication.

**Graded submodules.** A **graded submodule** of a graded left $A$-module $M$ is
a submodule $S\le M$ with $S=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}(S\cap M_d)$. Such an $S$
is itself a graded left $A$-module with homogeneous pieces
$S_d:=S\cap M_d$, because $A_iS_d\subseteq A_iM_d\cap S\subseteq M_{i+d}\cap S=S_{i+d}$;
equivalently, $S$ is generated by its homogeneous elements. In particular a
graded submodule is determined by its homogeneous pieces: if
$S=\bigoplus_dS_d$ and $T=\bigoplus_dT_d$ are graded submodules with $S_d=T_d$
for every $d$, then $S=T$.

**Internal shift.** For $r\in\mathbb Z$ and a graded module $M$, the
**internal shift** $M\{r\}$ is the module with

$$(M\{r\})_d:=M_{d-r}\qquad(d\in\mathbb Z),$$

carrying the same scalar action as $M$. Its components are additive subgroups
of $M$ whose sum is direct, so $M\{r\}$ is a $k$-module; and $M\{r\}$ is
graded because

$$A_i(M\{r\})_d=A_iM_{d-r}\subseteq M_{i+d-r}=(M\{r\})_{i+d}$$

for all $i,d$. For a graded bimodule both actions are unchanged, remain
homogeneous and still commute, so $M\{r\}$ is again a graded bimodule. The
shift is invertible: $(M\{r\})\{-r\}=M$, and $M\{0\}=M$. For a graded algebra
$A$, the shifts $A\{r\}$ of the regular bimodule are the modules denoted
$A\{r\}$ elsewhere on this page.

**Dictionary with the published twist.** In the published nonnegative
commutative convention ([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]]) the twist $M(a)$
is the graded module with $M(a)_d=M_{d+a}$ for every integer $a$. Substituting
$a=-r$ gives

$$(M\{r\})_d=M_{d-r}=M(-r)_d ,$$

so $M\{r\}=M(-r)$ as graded modules: the internal shift **reverses** the sign of
the published twist parameter. For $r=0$ both conventions agree with $M$.

**No super signs.** The internal degree is a genuine $\mathbb Z$-grading, not a
$\mathbb Z/2$-parity. No sign is inserted into the multiplication, the scalar
action or a degree-zero map merely because elements have nonzero degree; the
balancing relation of the tensor product below is likewise signed by nothing.
These are the unsigned associative conventions for this page; no differential
or signed symmetry on tensor products is part of this definition. They do not
exclude Koszul sign conventions in other categories of graded objects.

For the standard first-strand cyclotomic quotient of a real symmetrizable KLR
datum over any degree-zero field and every homogeneous (Q1)–(Q4) parameter
family, put $A=R^\Lambda(\beta)$, $B=R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$,
$e=e(\beta,i)$, $X=Be$, $Y=eB$,
$h=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$ and $t=2d_i(1-h)$.
There are explicit, compatible homogeneous maps
$$T_i:eBe\longrightarrow A,\qquad \deg T_i=t,$$
and finite homogeneous tensors
$$C_i=\sum_\alpha x_\alpha\otimes_A y_\alpha\in X\otimes_A Y,\qquad \deg x_\alpha+\deg y_\alpha=-t,$$
such that $T_i$ is an $A$-bimodule map, $bC_i=C_ib$ for every $b\in B$, and
$$x=\sum_\alpha x_\alpha T_i(y_\alpha x),\qquad y=\sum_\alpha T_i(yx_\alpha)y_\alpha.$$
In particular $X\{t\}\cong\operatorname{HOM}_A(Y,A)$ as $(B,A)$-bimodules,
where Hom is left-$A$-linear, the left $B$-action is precomposition with
right multiplication on $Y$, and the right $A$-action is multiplication on
values. The second unit is $b\mapsto bC_i$ and the second counit is
$y\otimes_B x\mapsto T_i(yx)$, giving
$E_i\{t\}\dashv F_i\dashv E_i$ on all graded modules. They are obtained by
finite normal-form/cap transport, not by assuming an actual Frobenius trace.
Dots and same-color crossing mates have the native cyclic normalization.
Each specified distinguished-$i$ different-color sideways pair has both
composites $t_{ij}$ times the identity. The separately distinguished-$j$
construction has both composites $t_{ji}$ times the identity. These are
different partial actions, not two different scalar values for the two
orders of one pair; their full word-closure comparison is not inferred here.
Arbitrary monic field specializations have the same ungraded construction,
with grading shifts forgotten. No finite-type, characteristic-zero,
geometric-global-basis or symmetric-trace premise is used.

Let $p(u)$ be monic of degree $N\geq0$ over a commutative ring $D$. Let $L_r$ be the monic factor ring $p=c_rb_{N-r}$, where $c_r$ is monic of degree $r$, and put $L_r=0$ for $r<0$ or $r>N$. Put
$$B_r=L_r[z]/b_{N-r}(z)=L_{r+1}[z]/c_{r+1}(z),\qquad h=N-2r.$$
Use the native nil-Hecke crossing $\tau=(1-s)/(X-Y)$ of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], dots of degree $2d$, and the matrix idempotent convention of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. Induction is $G(r)=B_r\{-2dr\}\otimes_{L_r}-$, basic restriction is the reversed $B_{r-1}$ tensor functor, and normalized restriction at input $r$ is $H(r)=B_{r-1}\{-d(1+h)\}\otimes_{L_r}-$. The first adjunction uses the coefficient form $\tau_{\rm new}:B_r\to L_{r+1}$ extracting $z^r$; the second uses $\tau_{\rm old}:B_r\to L_r$ extracting $z^{N-r-1}$. Units are the trace-dual power-basis Casimirs. Write $\eta:1\to HG$, $\varepsilon:GH\to1$, $\eta':1\to GH$, $\varepsilon':HG\to1$ for these maps, at their indicated input weights.

Set $P=GH$, $V=HG$ at input $r$. Define the actual native mates, rather than freely adjoined inverses, by
$$T=(HG\varepsilon)(H\tau^{GG}H)(\eta GH):P\to V,\qquad S=(GH\varepsilon')(G\tau^{HH}G)(\eta'HG):V\to P,$$
where $\tau^{HH}$ is the twofold first-adjunction mate of $\tau^{GG}$. Put
$$A(t)=t^h\frac{b(t^{-1})}{c(t^{-1})},\qquad \mathsf H(t)=A(t)^{-1},\qquad A_0=\mathsf H_0=1.$$
Coefficients with negative index are zero. For $h\geq0$, let $C_k=x^k\eta$ and
$$R_k=\sum_{a+j=h-1-k}A_j\varepsilon'x^a\quad(0\leq k<h).$$
Then the actual flag bimodule maps $\rho=(-T,C):P\oplus D_h\to V$ and $\sigma=(S,R):V\to P\oplus D_h$ satisfy
$$-ST=1_P,\quad R_kT=0,\quad SC_k=0,\quad R_kC_\ell=\delta_{k\ell},\quad -TS+\sum_kC_kR_k=1_V.$$
For $h<0$, set $C^-_k=x^k\eta'$ and
$$R^-_k=\sum_{a+j=-h-1-k}\mathsf H_j\varepsilon x^a\quad(0\leq k<-h).$$
The maps $\rho=(-T,R^-):P\to V\oplus D_{-h}$ and $\sigma=(S,C^-):V\oplus D_{-h}\to P$ satisfy
$$-TS=1_V,\quad TC^-_k=0,\quad R^-_kS=0,\quad R^-_kC^-_\ell=\delta_{k\ell},\quad -ST+\sum_kC^-_kR^-_k=1_P.$$
Here $D_h=\bigoplus_{k<h}1\{d(1-h+2k)\}$ and $D_{-h}=\bigoplus_{k<-h}1\{d(1+h+2k)\}$. At $h=0$ both sums are empty.

These maps also give the two typed upward curls
$$L_\mu=(H\varepsilon'_\mu)(\tau^{HH}G)(H\eta_\mu),\qquad R_\mu=(\varepsilon_\mu H)(G\tau^{HH})(\eta'_\mu H),$$
where $L_\mu$ has input $\mu$ and $R_\mu$ input $\mu-\alpha_i$, with $\langle h_i,\mu\rangle=h$. Their formulas are
$$L_\mu=\sum_{a+j=-h}x^a\mathsf H_j,\qquad R_\mu=-\sum_{a+j=h}x^aA_j.$$
All indices in these sums are nonnegative. Mating the two matrix-completeness equations gives the two opposite-crossing cancellation equations with literal-dot sum $a+b+c=-2$: the $HG$ boundary uses $A_{b+h+1}$, and the $GH$ boundary uses $\mathsf H_{b-h+1}$. **Total internal degree on the balanced tensor product.** Let $A$ be a graded

([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]). First use the canonical
decomposition of the ordinary tensor product of the underlying abelian groups
$$M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N\cong\bigoplus_{i,j\in\mathbb Z}M_i\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N_j.$$
Its inverse sends $m\otimes n$ to the finite sum
$\sum_{i,j}m_i\otimes n_j$, where $m=\sum_i m_i$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are their
homogeneous decompositions; the two maps are inverse because they agree with
the identity on homogeneous elementary tensors. Give the summand
$M_i\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N_j$ total degree $i+j$, and write
$G_d:=\bigoplus_{i+j=d}M_i\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N_j$.

The balanced tensor product
$M\otimes_AN=(M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N)/\mathcal R_A$
([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]), where
$\mathcal R_A$ is generated by the balance relations
$(ma)\otimes n-m\otimes(an)$. These relations are generated by the homogeneous
ones: for $m=\sum_i m_i$, $a=\sum_\ell a_\ell$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$, the relation
is the finite sum of
$(m_i a_\ell)\otimes n_j-m_i\otimes(a_\ell n_j)$ over $i,\ell,j$. Each such
homogeneous relation belongs to $G_{i+\ell+j}$, since the two module actions
preserve total degree. Thus $\mathcal R_A=\bigoplus_d(\mathcal R_A\cap G_d)$,
and

$$M\otimes_AN=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}(M\otimes_AN)_d,\qquad (M\otimes_AN)_d:=(G_d+\mathcal R_A)/\mathcal R_A,$$

is a graded abelian group. For homogeneous $m\in M_i$ and $n\in N_j$ the
elementary tensor $m\otimes n$ has **total internal degree** $i+j$; every tensor
is a finite sum of homogeneous elementary tensors, and the balancing relations
used in the quotient are homogeneous. This grading is the only grading used
below, and it introduces no sign.

**Outer actions.** If $M$ is a graded $(B,A)$-bimodule and $N$ a graded left
$A$-module, then the action $b(m\otimes n):=(bm)\otimes n$ of
[[thm-bimodule-actions-induced-on-tensor-products]] makes $M\otimes_AN$ a graded
left $B$-module: the action is homogeneous because homogeneous $b\in B_l$ sends
$m\otimes n$ of degree $i+j$ to an element of degree $l+i+j$. Symmetrically, if
$N$ is a graded $(A,C)$-bimodule, the action
$(m\otimes n)c:=m\otimes(nc)$ makes $M\otimes_AN$ a graded right $C$-module, and
the two outer actions commute when both are present.

**Homogeneous Hom.** For graded left $A$-modules $P,Q$, with
$\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(P,Q)$ the abelian group of all $A$-linear
maps $P\to Q$, put

$$\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,Q):=\bigl\{f\in\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(P,Q)\mid f(P_i)\subseteq Q_{i+d}\ \text{for all }i\in\mathbb Z\bigr\},\qquad \operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q):=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,Q).$$

Each $\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,Q)$ is a subgroup of
$\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(P,Q)$, and the sum is direct: if
$f=\sum_df_d=\sum_df'_d$ with $f_d,f'_d\in\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}$, then for
$p\in P_i$ the element $f(p)$ has homogeneous components
$f_d(p)\in Q_{i+d}$, and comparison of the graded components in $Q$ gives
$f_d(p)=f'_d(p)$ for every $d$ and $p$, so $f_d=f'_d$. Thus
$\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q)$ is a graded abelian group whose degree-$d$ part is
$\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,Q)$, and the degree-zero morphisms are
$\operatorname{Hom}_{A,0}(P,Q)$. By definition $\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q)$
consists of the finite sums of homogeneous $A$-linear maps, so
$\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q)\subseteq\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(P,Q)$
with equality only when every $A$-linear map has bounded spread in degree.

**The associative left action.** If $M$ is a graded $(B,A)$-bimodule and $Y$ a
graded left $B$-module, then $\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,Y)$ carries a left
$A$-module structure

$$(a\cdot f)(m):=f(ma)\qquad(a\in A,\ m\in M),$$

which is homogeneous: for $a\in A_i$ and $f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{B,d}(M,Y)$ one
has $ma\in M_{l+i}$ for $m\in M_l$, hence $(a\cdot f)(m)\in Y_{l+i+d}$ and
$a\cdot f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{B,d+i}(M,Y)$. The action is associative and
unital by the module axioms of $M$, so $\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,Y)$ is a graded
left $A$-module and an object of $\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$. The same formula
defines an action on the full ungraded $\operatorname{Hom}$ group, where it is
denoted by the same symbol.

**Ground ring and graded algebras.** Fix a commutative ring $k$. A **graded
$k$-algebra** is a $k$-algebra $A$ in the sense of
[[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]], together with a direct sum
decomposition of $k$-modules

$$A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb Z}A_i$$

such that $A_iA_j\subseteq A_{i+j}$ for all $i,j\in\mathbb Z$ and
$1_A\in A_0$. It is **unital and associative** when its underlying ring is;
every graded algebra on this page is unital and associative. Since
$\eta_A(r)=r\,1_A$ and $A_0$ is a $k$-submodule containing $1_A$, the structure
map has image in $A_0$, so each $A_i$ is a $k$-submodule and the scalars act
centrally on $A$.

**Graded modules and bimodules.** A **graded left $A$-module** is a left
$A$-module $M$ with a decomposition $M=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}M_d$ of
$k$-modules such that

$$A_iM_d\subseteq M_{i+d}\qquad\text{for all }i,d\in\mathbb Z .$$

A **graded right $A$-module** is a right $A$-module with a decomposition
$M=\bigoplus_dM_d$ such that $M_dA_i\subseteq M_{d+i}$ for all $i,d$. A
**graded $(B,A)$-bimodule** is a $(B,A)$-bimodule ([[def-bimodule]]) that is
graded as a $k$-module and homogeneous under both actions, the two actions
continuing to commute. Both induced $k$-actions must agree with the given
$k$-module structure: $\eta_B(t)m=tm=m\eta_A(t)$ for $t\in k$ and $m\in M$. Elements of $M_d$ are **homogeneous of degree $d$**, and
the decomposition expresses every $m\in M$ uniquely as a finite sum of nonzero
homogeneous components.

**Degree-zero maps.** A map $f:M\to N$ of graded left $A$-modules is
**degree-zero**, or a **graded map**, when it is $A$-linear and
$f(M_d)\subseteq N_d$ for every $d$. The category $\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$
has the graded left $A$-modules as objects and the degree-zero maps as
morphisms, with composition of maps. Every $M$ is an object of
$\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$ by its own grading, and $A$ is a graded
$(A,A)$-bimodule under left and right multiplication.

**Graded submodules.** A **graded submodule** of a graded left $A$-module $M$ is
a submodule $S\le M$ with $S=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}(S\cap M_d)$. Such an $S$
is itself a graded left $A$-module with homogeneous pieces
$S_d:=S\cap M_d$, because $A_iS_d\subseteq A_iM_d\cap S\subseteq M_{i+d}\cap S=S_{i+d}$;
equivalently, $S$ is generated by its homogeneous elements. In particular a
graded submodule is determined by its homogeneous pieces: if
$S=\bigoplus_dS_d$ and $T=\bigoplus_dT_d$ are graded submodules with $S_d=T_d$
for every $d$, then $S=T$.

**Internal shift.** For $r\in\mathbb Z$ and a graded module $M$, the
**internal shift** $M\{r\}$ is the module with

$$(M\{r\})_d:=M_{d-r}\qquad(d\in\mathbb Z),$$

carrying the same scalar action as $M$. Its components are additive subgroups
of $M$ whose sum is direct, so $M\{r\}$ is a $k$-module; and $M\{r\}$ is
graded because

$$A_i(M\{r\})_d=A_iM_{d-r}\subseteq M_{i+d-r}=(M\{r\})_{i+d}$$

for all $i,d$. For a graded bimodule both actions are unchanged, remain
homogeneous and still commute, so $M\{r\}$ is again a graded bimodule. The
shift is invertible: $(M\{r\})\{-r\}=M$, and $M\{0\}=M$. For a graded algebra
$A$, the shifts $A\{r\}$ of the regular bimodule are the modules denoted
$A\{r\}$ elsewhere on this page.

**Dictionary with the published twist.** In the published nonnegative
commutative convention ([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]]) the twist $M(a)$
is the graded module with $M(a)_d=M_{d+a}$ for every integer $a$. Substituting
$a=-r$ gives

$$(M\{r\})_d=M_{d-r}=M(-r)_d ,$$

so $M\{r\}=M(-r)$ as graded modules: the internal shift **reverses** the sign of
the published twist parameter. For $r=0$ both conventions agree with $M$.

**No super signs.** The internal degree is a genuine $\mathbb Z$-grading, not a
$\mathbb Z/2$-parity. No sign is inserted into the multiplication, the scalar
action or a degree-zero map merely because elements have nonzero degree; the
balancing relation of the tensor product below is likewise signed by nothing.
These are the unsigned associative conventions for this page; no differential
or signed symmetry on tensor products is part of this definition. They do not
exclude Koszul sign conventions in other categories of graded objects.

$\lambda_j\ge0$, impose $a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)=0$ and write $R^a(\beta)$ for the
resulting ordinary quotient. Then: every dot has a scalar-coefficient monic
annihilator in each fixed block; every $R^a(\beta)$ is finite dimensional over
$k$; and, for fixed $\beta$ and $i$, $R^a(\beta+m\alpha_i)=0$ for all
sufficiently large $m$. Thus right-append induction has finite $i$-strings. In
the standard homogeneous specialization $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$, every dot is
nilpotent and these are statements about the induced graded algebra and graded
functors. For an inhomogeneous monic specialization the assertions are
ungraded; no graded highest-weight Grothendieck identification is included.

For the standard first-strand cyclotomic KLR quotient over any degree-zero
field, any real symmetrizable datum, and every homogeneous (Q1)–(Q4)
parameter family, fix $B=R^\Lambda(\beta)$ and put
$t_\beta=(\beta,\beta)-2(\Lambda,\beta)$.
Compose the actual second caps of
[[lem-cyclotomic-klr-induction-restriction-bimodules-have-compatible-frobenius-dual-bases]]
along a word $\nu$ to obtain $\epsilon_\nu:e(\nu)Be(\nu)\to k$.
Then
$$\tau_\beta(a)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}\epsilon_\nu(e(\nu)ae(\nu))$$
is homogeneous of degree $t_\beta$, and
$a\mapsto[b\mapsto\tau_\beta(ba)]$ is an isomorphism
$B\to DB\{-t_\beta\}$. This proves perfectness of the actual word form,
including off-diagonal corner pairings, without assuming that a nonzero
closure detects every ideal.
For the native crossing $p_\nu=\tau_re(\nu)$ with bottom adjacent colors
$(i,j)$, $i\ne j$, and the $i$ strand directed SW to NE,

Dots, idempotents and same-color crossings have ratio $1$. The twofold
right-adjunction mate of $p_\nu$ has the same ratio to $p_\nu$; this is a
comparison of the actual separately constructed color adjunctions.
Choose a total order on the finite color support and set
$$c_\nu=\prod_{a<b,\,\nu_a>\nu_b}\frac{t_{\nu_a\nu_b}}{t_{\nu_b\nu_a}},\qquad c=\sum_\nu c_\nu e(\nu).$$
Then $\operatorname{tr}_\beta(a)=\tau_\beta(ca)$ is perfect and symmetric
of degree $t_\beta$, so $DB\cong B\{t_\beta\}$ as graded bimodules.

For the standard homogeneous first-strand cyclotomic quotient over any field
and every homogeneous (Q1)-(Q4) datum, use basic right-append induction $F_i$
from $\beta$ to $\beta+\alpha_i$ and basic restriction $E_i$ in the reverse
direction. Put $h=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$ and
$t_i(\beta)=2d_i(1-h)=(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)-2(\Lambda-\beta\mid\alpha_i)$.
Then there are explicit homogeneous bimodule units and counits with both
triangle identities giving $E_i\{t_i(\beta)\}\dashv F_i\dashv E_i$ on all
graded module categories. They preserve the standard dot-cyclic and same-color
crossing-mate identities and the coherent different-color double-mate
identity: for $p_\nu=\tau_re(\nu)$ with bottom adjacent colors $(i,j)$,
$i\ne j$, its double right mate is $(t_{ij}/t_{ji})p_\nu$, where $t_{ij}$ is
the coefficient of $u^{-a_{ij}}$ in $Q_{ij}(u,v)$ and the strand of color $i$
runs SW to NE. Equivalently the associated right closure satisfies
$\operatorname{cl}(p_\nu a)=(t_{ij}/t_{ji})\operatorname{cl}(ap_\nu)$ for
$a\in e(\nu)R^\Lambda(\beta)e(s_r\nu)$; dots, idempotents and equal-color

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $\psi$ be the horizontal-reflection anti-involution of $R(\beta)$ (reflection of diagrams about a horizontal axis, which reverses the order of crossings); for a finitely generated graded left module $P$ let $P^{\psi}$ be the right module with $p\cdot r:=\psi(r)p$. For $\beta\in Q_+$ define the **Cartan pairing**
$$([P],[Q])_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\bigl(P^{\psi}\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q\bigr)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q,\qquad (\beta)_q:=\prod_i\prod_{a=1}^{\beta_i}\frac1{1-q^{2d_i a}},$$
for finitely generated graded projective modules $P,Q$, where $\mathrm{gdim}_kM=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}q^m\dim_kM_m$; the tensor is over the graded algebra with the total-degree grading ([[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]]). Equivalently define the **hom pairing** $([P],[Q])'_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,Q)$ ([[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]], [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]]); then $([P],[Q])'_\beta=([P^\#],[Q])_\beta$ for the graded left projective $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$. Thus the tensor form is symmetric and bilinear; the Hom form is conjugate-linear in its first variable and linear in its second. For the tensor form $([P],q[Q])=q([P],[Q])$ and $(q[P],[Q])=q([P],[Q])$, while the Hom form obeys $h(q^r[P],q^s[Q])=q^{s-r}h([P],[Q])$. Both are additive, vanish on different-weight components, and descend to $K_0(R)=\bigoplus_\beta K_0(R(\beta))$: the tensor form is $A$-bilinear and the Hom form is $A$-sesquilinear (first variable conjugate-linear), with values in $\mathbb Q(q)$, more precisely in the localization adjoining all $(1-q_i^{2a})^{-1}$; the values lie in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q$ because $P^\psi\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q$ is a finite free graded module over the central color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra $C_\beta$ of [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]. Normalization: $([P_i],[P_i])=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}$ and $([P_i],[P_j])=0$ for $i\ne j$, where $P_i=R(\alpha_i)$.

Fix a graded $k$-algebra $A$ and let $P$ be a graded left $A$-module
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]). The category
$\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$ of graded left $A$-modules and degree-zero maps is
abelian ([[lem-graded-module-kernels-cokernels-and-biproducts-are-degreewise]]).

**Graded projective.** $P$ is **graded projective** when it is a projective
object of $\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$ ([[def-projective-object]]): for every
degree-zero epimorphism $q:E\twoheadrightarrow M$ and every degree-zero
$f:P\to M$ there exists a degree-zero $\widetilde f:P\to E$ with
$q\widetilde f=f$. Thus projectivity is tested only against degree-zero
epimorphisms and degree-zero maps, and the lift need not be unique.

**Finitely generated.** $P$ is **finitely generated as a graded left
$A$-module**, or generated by finitely many homogeneous elements, when for some
$n\ge0$ there are homogeneous elements $p_1,\dots,p_n\in P$ with

$$P=A p_1+\cdots+A p_n .$$

By [[def-generated-cyclic-finitely-generated-and-free-modules]] this is the same
notion as finite generation of the underlying $A$-module: a finite homogeneous
family is a finite family, and conversely, if $P=\langle S\rangle_A$ for a
finite set $S$, then writing each $s=\sum_es_e$ as its finite sum of nonzero
homogeneous components gives, for every $x=\sum_{s\in S}a_s s\in P$,

$$x=\sum_{s\in S}a_s\sum_es_e=\sum_{s,e}a_s s_e,$$

a finite $A$-linear combination of the homogeneous elements $s_e\in P$; so the
finitely many components of the members of $S$ generate $P$. In particular the
notion does not depend on the chosen finite generating set.

**Finite graded projective.** $P$ is **finite graded projective** when it is
graded projective and generated by finitely many homogeneous elements, that is,
when it is graded projective and finitely generated as an $A$-module. The family
may be empty: $n=0$ gives $P=Ap_1+\cdots+Ap_n=0$, so the zero module is
generated by the empty homogeneous family, and the corresponding finite direct
sum of shifts in the characterization below is the empty direct sum. Its finite
shifted-free characterization is the next result
([[thm-finite-graded-projectives-are-summands-of-finite-graded-free-modules]]),
and it uses this same notion of finite generation throughout: a finite
homogeneous generating family there is exactly a family as above. No choice
principle is used in the equivalence above, which only rewrites a given finite
expression.

**Ground ring and graded algebras.** Fix a commutative ring $k$. A **graded
$k$-algebra** is a $k$-algebra $A$ in the sense of
[[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]], together with a direct sum
decomposition of $k$-modules

$$A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb Z}A_i$$

such that $A_iA_j\subseteq A_{i+j}$ for all $i,j\in\mathbb Z$ and
$1_A\in A_0$. It is **unital and associative** when its underlying ring is;
every graded algebra on this page is unital and associative. Since
$\eta_A(r)=r\,1_A$ and $A_0$ is a $k$-submodule containing $1_A$, the structure
map has image in $A_0$, so each $A_i$ is a $k$-submodule and the scalars act
centrally on $A$.

**Graded modules and bimodules.** A **graded left $A$-module** is a left
$A$-module $M$ with a decomposition $M=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}M_d$ of
$k$-modules such that

$$A_iM_d\subseteq M_{i+d}\qquad\text{for all }i,d\in\mathbb Z .$$

A **graded right $A$-module** is a right $A$-module with a decomposition
$M=\bigoplus_dM_d$ such that $M_dA_i\subseteq M_{d+i}$ for all $i,d$. A
**graded $(B,A)$-bimodule** is a $(B,A)$-bimodule ([[def-bimodule]]) that is
graded as a $k$-module and homogeneous under both actions, the two actions
continuing to commute. Both induced $k$-actions must agree with the given
$k$-module structure: $\eta_B(t)m=tm=m\eta_A(t)$ for $t\in k$ and $m\in M$. Elements of $M_d$ are **homogeneous of degree $d$**, and
the decomposition expresses every $m\in M$ uniquely as a finite sum of nonzero
homogeneous components.

**Degree-zero maps.** A map $f:M\to N$ of graded left $A$-modules is
**degree-zero**, or a **graded map**, when it is $A$-linear and
$f(M_d)\subseteq N_d$ for every $d$. The category $\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$
has the graded left $A$-modules as objects and the degree-zero maps as
morphisms, with composition of maps. Every $M$ is an object of
$\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$ by its own grading, and $A$ is a graded
$(A,A)$-bimodule under left and right multiplication.

**Graded submodules.** A **graded submodule** of a graded left $A$-module $M$ is
a submodule $S\le M$ with $S=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}(S\cap M_d)$. Such an $S$
is itself a graded left $A$-module with homogeneous pieces
$S_d:=S\cap M_d$, because $A_iS_d\subseteq A_iM_d\cap S\subseteq M_{i+d}\cap S=S_{i+d}$;
equivalently, $S$ is generated by its homogeneous elements. In particular a
graded submodule is determined by its homogeneous pieces: if
$S=\bigoplus_dS_d$ and $T=\bigoplus_dT_d$ are graded submodules with $S_d=T_d$
for every $d$, then $S=T$.

**Internal shift.** For $r\in\mathbb Z$ and a graded module $M$, the
**internal shift** $M\{r\}$ is the module with

$$(M\{r\})_d:=M_{d-r}\qquad(d\in\mathbb Z),$$

carrying the same scalar action as $M$. Its components are additive subgroups
of $M$ whose sum is direct, so $M\{r\}$ is a $k$-module; and $M\{r\}$ is
graded because

$$A_i(M\{r\})_d=A_iM_{d-r}\subseteq M_{i+d-r}=(M\{r\})_{i+d}$$

for all $i,d$. For a graded bimodule both actions are unchanged, remain
homogeneous and still commute, so $M\{r\}$ is again a graded bimodule. The
shift is invertible: $(M\{r\})\{-r\}=M$, and $M\{0\}=M$. For a graded algebra
$A$, the shifts $A\{r\}$ of the regular bimodule are the modules denoted
$A\{r\}$ elsewhere on this page.

**Dictionary with the published twist.** In the published nonnegative
commutative convention ([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]]) the twist $M(a)$
is the graded module with $M(a)_d=M_{d+a}$ for every integer $a$. Substituting
$a=-r$ gives

$$(M\{r\})_d=M_{d-r}=M(-r)_d ,$$

so $M\{r\}=M(-r)$ as graded modules: the internal shift **reverses** the sign of
the published twist parameter. For $r=0$ both conventions agree with $M$.

**No super signs.** The internal degree is a genuine $\mathbb Z$-grading, not a
$\mathbb Z/2$-parity. No sign is inserted into the multiplication, the scalar
action or a degree-zero map merely because elements have nonzero degree; the
balancing relation of the tensor product below is likewise signed by nothing.
These are the unsigned associative conventions for this page; no differential
or signed symmetry on tensor products is part of this definition. They do not
exclude Koszul sign conventions in other categories of graded objects.
